name: Brownish Purple Red
lede: Brownish Purple Red is entry 97 among the reds in Werner's nomenclature of colours, a dusty rose-brown that the book matched to a bat's wing.

sections.title: Entry 97
sections.body:
Brownish Purple Red is number 97 in the red series of the colour nomenclature reproduced in Baty's book on nature's palette [1]. It sits between Veinous Blood Red (96) and Chocolate Red (98), after a run of crimson and cochineal reds [1][2].

The nomenclature describes each color by living examples. For this one the book shows the wings of a bat, drawn from a zoological voyage report of the 1840s [3]. Its neighbor Chocolate Red is matched to the breast feathers of a bird of paradise [3].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The swatch is sampled from an aged copy of Werner's chart, so it is approximate [4]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 system places it in "light grayish reddish brown", about 6 units of color difference away [4]. Neighbors on the screen are [[brownish-red]] and [[mauve]], which is pinker [4][5].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The ColorHub archive files this swatch with the neutrals: lightness about 51 out of 100 and a chroma of only 11 [4]. Contrast against white is 4.32 to 1 [4].
